note: The two directions of public-surface debt, enumerated. Consumed by tests/livespec_runtime/test_public_surface_inventory.py. unratified_modules carries the shipped-but-unratified direction: the test fails when a module exports names, carries no ratified section in SPECIFICATION/contracts.md, and is absent from that list. ratified_unshipped_modules carries the reverse: a section ratified AHEAD of its module, waiving the test's phantom-section and phantom-name legs for that one module while the row names it and an owning work-item. Both registers SHRINK. A ratified_unshipped_modules row is the ONE row that may be added, and only by the revise that ratifies its section; every other change to either list is a DELETION (when the module is ratified, declared internal, stops exporting, or starts shipping). A row that no longer describes the tree is a stale-row failure.
authority: SPECIFICATION/spec.md, section "Public surface": "Every shipped module that declares a public surface is inside the ratified inventory or is explicitly declared internal there. ... A module that ships a public surface and appears in neither place is a defect rather than tolerated debt, and tests/livespec_runtime/test_public_surface_inventory.py fails on it; the `# @generated` third-party port that test's register excludes is outside this rule by construction." The per-family disposition that drained unratified_modules to empty is in plan/runtime-backlog-drain/research/005-mqsxsu4-public-surface-reconciliation.md. ratified_unshipped_modules is authorized by the converse clause of the same section, ratified as v026 by proposal ratified-unshipped-module-register: "Such a section MAY name a module that does not ship yet only while a row of the `ratified_unshipped_modules` register in `tests/public-surface-debt.json` names that module and a live owning work-item. ... A row MAY be added only by the revise that ratifies its section, and otherwise the register only shrinks: the change that ships the module MUST delete its row, a row whose module now ships MUST fail the suite as stale, and the owning work-item MUST NOT close while its row stands." That last obligation is LEDGER state the test cannot read, so it is a manual obligation on the revise and the owning work-item, not a promise this file makes.

generated_ports.reason: Verbatim third-party port carried source-only, marked `# @generated` by 0ad3f8c so is_generated() drops it uniformly from every structural check's first-party universe. Its `__all__` is livespec-added conformance metadata over upstream bytes, not a declaration of this library's surface; the ratified surface for the algorithm is the keyword-only wrapper in livespec_runtime/work_items/rank.py. Editing the file to drop `BASE_62_DIGITS` / `FIError` would deviate the port from upstream to restate what the universe rule already says.
